newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon property tax revenue up despite price fall.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon property tax revenue up despite price fall.

text.p: Lebanese government revenues from taxation of property deals rose by nearly a third in the first 10 months of 1996 despite a drop in property prices, now about 20 percent down from the start of the year.
A rush to register previous deals helped boost revenues, a finance ministry official said on Wednesday.
The ministry said it collected $124 million in taxes on property sales compared with $94.61 million in the first 10 months of 1995.
In October alone it collected $17.68 million compared with $11.97 million in the same month in 1995.

Tax rates on property deals vary from district to district, but average about 6.5 percent. However, tax collection does not truly reflect the state of the market because deals are sometimes understated to avoid tax, property analysts said.

The rise in tax this year came from increased volume of deals and despite a drop in property prices, which are now as much as 20 percent below their level at the start of the year, according to estimates by analysts.
Private economist and consultant Marwan Iskander said construction permits dropped 66 percent in the first nine months of the year.

The property market would have fallen further but for injections of capital totalling $300 million through a $100 million facility from the World Bank's International Finance Corporation and through measures taken by the central bank to boost lending to the sector, Iskander said.
The dollar figures are based on an exchange rate of 1556 Lebanese pounds in October 1996 compared with 1605 in October 1995.
